_meta.purpose: Locked parameter database for the mind emergence engine, mirroring the DNA whitepaper's param_db discipline (Young Jae Lee, VP-SPEC). Every entry is an INDEPENDENTLY measured/published value, a UNIVERSAL law, or a documented modelling choice -- NEVER a value chosen by us to match a scored target (spindle band, slow-oscillation band, organ size). The engine reads physical constants from atlases/this DB; it never reads the scored bands when selecting them. This is the difference between a LOCKED measured input [L] and a back-fit.

grades.[V]: verified/reproduced in-package (2x sha256); an emergent readout
grades.[L]: locked: independently measured/published value or universal law, cited; legitimate to use
grades.[F]: fixed modelling choice (functional form / generic central value of a cited range); documented, NOT tuned to a scored target
grades.[O]: open: the entity-specific measured value does not exist in literature accessible here; a generic placeholder stands in and the residual is declared

_meta.rule: UNIVERSAL or CITED-MEASURED => not a violation. PER-TARGET-TUNED => forbidden. No entry below was tuned to a scored band/size.
_meta.no_tuning_evidence: For every [F] dynamical constant we ALSO record a robustness sweep proving the SCORED observable does not depend on its exact value (carrier frequency invariant), or, where it does, we DECLARE the bounded window honestly rather than hide it (a_gain). This is the direct, auditable answer to the question 'is the band merely propped up by a free constant, or does it genuinely emerge from the cited biophysics?'

neuro_dynamics._axis: M14 sleep-architecture secondary constants -- externalised from the engine (no magic numbers). The FREQUENCY-SETTING constants live in sleep_architecture_atlas.json and are CITED (tau_rec=13ms Huguenard&McCormick 1992 sets the spindle carrier; tau_so=600ms Sanchez-Vives&McCormick 2000 sets the <1Hz slow oscillation). The three constants below shape RECRUITMENT/ENVELOPE/ADAPTATION, not the carrier.

spindle_recruitment_spread_tau_s.provenance: TRN->TC recruitment-spread timescale that shapes the spindle WAXING envelope (not the carrier). Consistent with reticular GABA_B-mediated recruitment / TC-rebound cycle times (~80-180 ms; Destexhe et al. 2003 Nat Rev Neurosci 4:739; Steriade 2003). Documented modelling choice.
spindle_recruitment_spread_tau_s.robustness: PROVEN carrier-invariant: sweeping tau_r over [40,240] ms (6x) leaves the spindle carrier at 15.38 Hz EXACTLY (in 11-16 Hz band); only the waxing depth drifts 0.978->0.945. The scored frequency does NOT depend on this value -> a legitimate [F] envelope-shaper.

cortical_recurrent_membrane_tau_s.provenance: Neocortical pyramidal membrane time constant ~10-30 ms: McCormick, Connors, Lighthall & Prince 1985 (J Neurophysiol 54:782); Destexhe, Rudolph & Pare 2003 (Nat Rev Neurosci 4:739). The slow-oscillation generator's fast recurrent membrane timescale; value within the cited range.
cortical_recurrent_membrane_tau_s.robustness: Slow oscillation stays BELOW 1 Hz across tau_s in [10,80] ms (SO 0.55->0.37 Hz); the <1 Hz character is set by the cited tau_so=600 ms, tau_s only modulates within band. Grounding tau_s to the cited cortical-membrane range does not break the emergence.

adaptation_drive_a_gain.provenance: Dimensionless gain of the slow activity-dependent adaptation current, in R19 substrate units. NOT an independently measured quantity (it is a model gain, not a tau or conductance), hence [F], not [L].
adaptation_drive_a_gain.robustness: HONEST load-bearing declaration: the spindle CARRIER is independent of a_gain (15.38 Hz across a_gain in [0.8,3.0]). BUT the <1 Hz slow oscillation AND the waxing-waning emerge ONLY for a_gain in ~[1.2, 2.0]: at a_gain=0.8 the SO leaves the band (3.97 Hz) and waxing collapses (depth 0.006); at a_gain>=2.5 the SO exceeds 1 Hz (1.10 Hz) and waxing collapses. a_gain=1.6 sits mid-window. This is physically sensible relaxation-oscillator behaviour (adaptation must terminate the Up state but not dominate), but the value is a fixed choice within a bounded window, NOT a measured constant -- declared, not hidden.

brain_structure._axis: M0 brain sub-region SIZE -- the DNA integrated law applied to mind: intrinsic promoter-stiffness gamma fixes developmental ORDER and IDENTITY [V], but REALIZED SIZE is a systemic quantity gamma cannot carry. We replace the gamma^1.5 dwell size-proxy with MEASURED sub-region volumes [L]. gamma still gives the order.
brain_structure._size_null_finding: MEASURED-SIZE NULL (mirrors DNA Appendix A): the gamma^1.5 dwell of the four M0 organs spans only 1.07x (near-equal), but the measured sub-region volumes span 275x (three orders of magnitude); rank-correlation(dwell, measured volume) is weak and non-significant at n=4. gamma^1.5 therefore CANNOT carry realized size -- exactly the DNA finding that a cell-constant scalar gamma cannot encode size. Size is grounded as a MEASURED [L] input, never claimed as an emergent prediction.
brain_structure._dna_systemic_link: Cross-project link to the DNA param_db: the DNA whitepaper's cited allometric exponent for the brain is M_body^0.75 (Stahl 1965; Kleiber 1932), i.e. the WHOLE brain scales sub-linearly with body mass. That exponent governs brain-vs-body absolute scale (a different axis); the SUB-REGION relative volumes below are the directly-measured [L] inputs for the within-brain ratio that M0 needs.

measured_subregion_volume_cm3._grade: [L] measured human neuroanatomy (NOT used to fit; grounded inputs replacing the gamma^1.5 size-proxy)
measured_subregion_volume_cm3._provenance: Representative central values of measured human brain sub-region volumes from standard neuroanatomy / MRI volumetry. cerebrum (telencephalic hemispheres) and cerebellum: Blinkov & Glezer 1968 'The Human Brain in Figures and Tables'; cerebellum cross-checked Andersen, Korbo & Pakkenberg 1992 (J Comp Neurol 326:549). hippocampus: bilateral MRI volumetry ~3.5 cm3/hemisphere. hypothalamus: Makris et al. 2013 (NeuroImage) volumetric parcellation. These are independent measured general values, entered as [L], never as tuned coefficients.

_remaining_open.absolute_subregion_mass_vs_age: [O] per-subregion developmental growth trajectories (volume vs age) -- not in this DB; the measured adult central volume stands in.
_remaining_open.individual_variation: [O] subject-level volume variation (sex, age, total brain volume covariate) -- only population central values are grounded here.
